'''Ernst Lebrecht Henneberg''' (27 September 1850 – 29 April 1933)<ref name=LAGIS>{{Cite web |title=Hessian Biography : Index Search : LAGIS Hessen |url=https://www.lagis-hessen.de/en/subjects/rsrec/sn/bio/register/person/entry/henneberg%252C+heinrich |access-date=2023-05-20 |website=www.lagis-hessen.de}}</ref> was a German professor of mechanics and {{Citation needed span|text=applied|date=May 2023|reason=APPLIED mathematics is mentioned in DNB, and is not sourced in the "Life" section below}} [[mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-20 |title=Katalog der Deutschen Nationalbibliothek |url=https://portal.dnb.de/opac.htm?method=simpleSearch&cqlMode=true&query=nid%3D116710802 |access-date=2023-05-20 |website=German National Library}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |title=The Econometric Society: Notes on Contributions |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1933-39-09/S0002-9904-1933-05717-8/S0002-9904-1933-05717-8.pdf |journal=Econometrica |page=666 |via=American Mathematical Society}}</ref>

== Life ==
Ernst Lebrecht Henneberg was born in [[Wolfenbüttel]] in 1850 to Heinrich Henneberg and Sophie Rimpau.<ref name=HC>{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |title=Award List: "Honorary Cross of the Order of Merit of Philip the Magnanimous" (Grand Duchy of Hesse, 1900–1918) |url=https://www.deutsche-gesellschaft-fuer-ordenskunde.de/DGOWP/wp-content/uploads/2016/04/Verleih_Liste_Ehrenkreuz_Philipps-Orden_Adler.pdf |access-date=March 25, 2025 |website=German Society for the Study of Orders (e.V.) Association for Phaleristics}}</ref> From 1870 until 1876 he studied mathematics in [[Zürich]], [[Heidelberg]], and [[Berlin]], receiving his doctorate in 1875 from [[Hermann Schwarz]] while in Zürich.<ref name=HC /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lebrecht |first=Henneberg |date=1876 |title=Heber diejenige Minimalfläche, welche die Neil'sche Parabel zur ebenen geodätischen Linie hat |url=https://archive.org/details/vierteljahrsschr21natu/page/66/mode/2up?view=theater |journal=[[Quarterly Journal of the Natural Research Society in Zurich]] |language=German |pages=66–70 |via=Internet Archive}}</ref>{{Verify source|date=May 2023}} After living in Zürich from 1876 until 1878, he became an associate professor for [[Descriptive geometry|descriptive]] and [[synthetic geometry]] and [[graphic statics]] at [[Technische Universität Darmstadt|TU Darmstat]]. Not soon after in 1879, he became a professor of mechanics at the university.<ref name=HC />

From 1887 to 1890 Henneberg was the dean of the [[Electrical engineering|Electrical Engineering]] school at TU Darmstat. In 1888, Henneburg was elected as a member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|Leopoldina]].<ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |title=Member Directory |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/lebrecht-henneberg/ |access-date=March 25, 2025 |website=Leopoldina}}</ref> By 1890, he was one of the founders of the German Association of Mathematicians. From 1890 to 1891 Henneberg had become the dean of the Mathematics and Sciences school, while also acting as the [[Rector (academia)|rector]] from 1891 to 1893.<ref name=LAGIS />

In 1903 he went on to write an article on graph theory in the Encyclopedia of Mathematical Sciences. The Henneberg's method of bar conversion and the [[Henneberg surface|Henneberg minimum surface]] that he found in his dissertation are named after him.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |title=Henneberg's Minimal Surface |url=https://demonstrations.wolfram.com/HennebergsMinimalSurface/ |access-date=March 25, 2025 |website=Wolfram Demonstrations Project}}</ref>

During both 1902-1905 and 1911-14 he was Dean of the General Department, and on September 30, 1920, he retired from this position.<ref name=HC /> In 1933, Ernst died a professor in the department of Mechanics at TU Darmstadt.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=September 1933 |title=The Econometric Society Journal |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1933-39-09/S0002-9904-1933-05717-8/S0002-9904-1933-05717-8.pdf |access-date=March 25, 2025 |website=American Mathematical Society}}</ref>

Henneberg was married to Pauline Grunewald; their daughter Paula married the geologist [[Werner Janensch]].<ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |title=Werner Janensch |url=https://www.deutsche-biographie.de/gnd117078166.html#ndbcontent |access-date=March 25, 2025 |website=Deutsche Biographie}}</ref>

== Honors ==
1892 November 25: Award of the Knight's Cross 1st Class of the Order of Merit of [[Philip I, Landgrave of Hesse|Philip the Magnanimous]]<ref name=HC />

1898 November 25: Appointment as Privy Councilor<ref name=HC />

1904 November 25 Award of the Cross of Honor of the Order of Merit of Philip the Magnanimous

1911: PhD of engineering at the Technical University of Braunschweig.

1917 March 13: Awarded the Commander's Cross II. Class of the Order of Merit of Philip the Magnanimous<ref name=HC />

1925: Honorary Senator at TH Darmstadt.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |title=Honorary Senators |url=https://www.tu-darmstadt.de/universitaet/organisation_verwaltung/geschichte_persoenlichkeiten/ehrensenatoren_und_ehrensenatorinnen/index.en.jsp |access-date=March 25, 2025 |website=TU Darmstadt}}</ref>
